transcript:
Header: 2026-06-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Aisha (CTO Momentum Labs), Tom (Lead ML Eng), Sara (SRE)

00:00 Jamie: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro — I'm Jamie, AE at Redwood, and with me is Carlos from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
00:12 Aisha: Good, thanks. Excited to learn how quick this quickstart actually is, we want to try the hosted API first.
00:20 Carlos: Awesome; goal for today — walk through self-serve flow, free credits, and answer any infra/compliance Qs. We'll cover time-to-first-token and options for Dedicated/Private for production.
00:35 Tom: Great. For context, our infra: most of our stack is on GCP, some on-prem for regulated workloads. We use Istio and have a proxy-based egress policy, and our latency SLO is 120ms p95 for inference.
00:52 Jamie: Good, that helps. Quick question on volume — are you primarily bursts from a web app or steady stream?
01:00 Tom: Mostly bursty, user-facing features — chat and summarization. Peak about 120 QPS, average maybe 10 QPS.
01:12 Sara: And we need data not to be persisted by vendors for training — i.e., no retention, logs only for billing.
01:21 Jamie: Understood — Redwood Hosted has opt-out for data retention and a privacy mode; for stricter needs we can talk Private with customer-managed KMS.
01:35 Aisha: Can you clarify free credits and how fast we can get to first token? We want to hand this to two engineers and see results same day.
01:45 Carlos: Absolutely. With self-serve you can sign up and get free credits instantly. Typical time-to-first-token is under 10 minutes if you follow the quickstart: API key, SDK install, and a small sample request. We'll send a quickstart guide that maps to your stack (GCP).
02:02 Tom: Nice. For code-level: does Redwood SDK auto-stream? We care about streaming for chat UIs.
02:12 Carlos: Yes — streaming responses are supported in the hosted API like other providers. There's also function/tool calling and structured outputs. The SDK examples include node/python streaming snippets.
02:28 Aisha: What about production? We like the idea of Dedicated capacity for predictability. How does that compare cost-wise vs hosted?
02:39 Jamie: Good question. Hosted is pay-as-you-go — lower upfront but variable unit cost. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with committed monthly spend — more predictable per-token pricing and isolation. For heavy sustained traffic Dedicated usually lowers unit cost. We can run quick numbers after we see your traffic profile.
02:58 Tom: And Private (VPC/on-prem)? We have one HIPAA-adjacent initiative where data can't leave our VPC.
03:07 Carlos: Private supports VPC peering and an on-prem package. It also supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. There's more ops lift but it removes vendor data egress concerns.
03:22 Sara: Any SOC2 or ISO reports we can see?
03:28 Jamie: Yes — we'll share SOC2 Type II and our security whitepaper. Also the network architecture doc that shows VPC options.
03:36 Aisha: Great. Can you do an initial latency benchmark? We may want to test both hosted and Dedicated variants.
03:44 Carlos: We can — for hosted, it's usually fastest to do a quick test from your region; Dedicated will be measured based on the instance types you commit to. We'll propose a micro-benchmark: 50 short prompts, 50 long prompts, measure p50/p95 and throughput.
04:02 Tom: Sounds good. Do you support KV cache or prefix caching? That's important for conversational state.
04:10 Carlos: We do KV cache and prefix caching to reduce token cost and latency; sometimes the SE doc shows it as key-value or "kay-vee" cache in the notes — apologies for the auto-transcript noise.
04:25 Aisha: Heh, no worries. On auth: does Redwood integrate with our SSO (SAML) for team accounts and RBAC?
04:33 Jamie: Yes, SSO/SAML and granular RBAC for team roles. For Dedicated/Private we support enterprise SSO and SCIM provisioning.
04:44 Sara: Any typical gotchas with GCP egress and network policies?
04:50 Carlos: Two things — ensure firewall allows egress to Redwood endpoints or peering config for VPC; and if you're in a private setup, you'll likely set up VPC peering and route tables. We'll share a checklist.
05:05 Tom: What about model choices — do you host open models and any Redwood-curated models?
05:12 Carlos: We have a model catalog with curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. For PLG quickstarts we expose a small set optimized for latency and cost.
05:25 Aisha: If we start with hosted during evaluation and later move to Dedicated, what's the migration friction?
05:31 Jamie: Minimal — same API surface and SDKs. We support pinning model versions and rollouts so you can canary between hosted and dedicated or roll traffic over. Smart routing helps with fallback.
05:45 Tom: On billing: do you show token-level cost breakdowns? Need per-route and per-model dash for cost ops.
05:53 Jamie: Yes — Redwood Console offers token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-route dashboards. You can also set quotas.
06:04 Aisha: About free credits — is there an expiration and can we use them for Dedicated POC?
06:11 Jamie: Free credits typically apply to the hosted API. For Dedicated POCs we can set up a time-limited trial arrangement; we'll coordinate with Sales Ops.
06:21 Tom: Regarding latency — our web UI needs streaming and p95 <= 120ms. If hosted p95 is higher, we might need a Dedicated pin or edge region. Does Redwood have regional endpoints?
06:33 Carlos: Yes, multi-region support. You can route by region and we can place Dedicated pools in the cloud region closest to your traffic. Also caching reduces effective latency for repeated prompts.
06:47 Aisha: Any rate limiting on the free tier?
06:51 Jamie: Free credits come with lower default quotas; you can request higher rate limits for POC.
06:59 Tom: For the benchmark, I'd like to test both streaming and non-streaming paths, and quantify cost per 1k tokens.
07:07 Carlos: We'll include cost-per-token estimates in the benchmark spreadsheet. We'll also show quantization and batching knobs that reduce cost for high throughput.
07:19 Aisha: How long does it take to onboard devs? We want 2 engineers to be productive same day.
07:25 Jamie: Typically under an hour to get a first request; with our quickstart + SDK and example notebooks, many teams hit first token in <10 minutes. We'll send example snippets keyed to Node/Python.
07:38 Tom: Any quirks in the quickstart for service accounts, env variables, proxy?
07:44 Carlos: There are steps for env var names and optional proxy config — we'll provide a GCP-specific quickstart note since you mentioned Istio and egress policies.
07:55 Aisha: On logs, can we disable request/response logging for hosted?
08:00 Jamie: Yes you can opt-out of retention; request logs needed for debugging can be retained but we can limit retention window or mask PII.
08:10 Sara: One security question: for Dedicated and Private, where are keys stored? KMS only?
08:15 Carlos: For Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we can also integrate with your KMS depending on deployment.
08:26 Aisha: Okay, next steps from our side: Tom to share traffic profile and latency targets; Sara to make sure network folks are available for a VPC checklist meeting.
08:35 Jamie: And we'll send the quickstart, free credits, SOC2 and recommended benchmark plan. Carlos will run the 30-min demo/benchmark with Tom.

[Conversation continues with deeper technical clarifications and occasional cross-talk]

15:12 Tom: One more — do you support model quantization or smaller footprints to reduce cost?
15:18 Carlos: Yes, Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles and kernel selection; our runtime supports quantized variants. We'll show expected perf delta in the benchmark sheet.
15:35 Aisha: If we do a Dedicated commit, what's a typical SLA?
15:40 Jamie: SLA depends on the contract but Dedicated comes with uptime and latency targets; we can include a premium SLA for enterprise deals.
15:52 Sara: Are there white-glove migration services?
15:55 Jamie: Yes, Professional Services or Solutions Engineering engagements for migrations.

[Final recap]

42:10 Jamie: Recap — send quickstart + credits, SOC2 and network doc, benchmark plan; Carlos to run a demo/bench with Tom next week; Tom to share traffic profile. Any other Qs?
42:25 Aisha: No that's it, thanks.
42:30 Tom: Thanks everyone.
42:35 Jamie: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with materials and proposed times.

End of transcript. Some auto-transcript errors present (names/terms occasionally mis-typed).

Shared artifacts referenced: quickstart.pdf (link in email), benchmark-template.xlsx (link), security-whitepaper.pdf (link).
